conditions: T3 vaults spawn three enemy Necramechs per run (1.5 expected parts) versus one in T1; clear T1 and T2 once each first, they stay unlocked permanently.

disclosures.title: Requiem Obelisks beat mining and fishing
disclosures.body: Shoot the Reactive Crystal with Operator Void damage to start a 90-second obelisk; kills from your Operator, a Necramech, or an Umbra specter while you're in Operator drop Cambion Drift mining and fishing resources directly, no drill or spear. Warframe kills give nothing. Use a weak amp to conserve the obelisk's health, group enemies into its radius, and only trigger the Khra, Ris, Vome or Fass symbols; Lohk, Netra, Jahu and Xata don't reliably pay out. Running one inside a vault (before the Reactive Crystal stage) gives an endless spawn window instead of the surface's four-group, 10-minute-cooldown limit.

bonuses: Cave veins farther from the Necralisk report more resources per node than the ones close to the hub.
Rolizor and Spitia Infested cysts drop Adramalium; Auroron Entrati caskets and Requiem Pylons drop Biotic Filter — a max-range looter frame sweeping the surface picks both up in bulk.

disclosures.title: most guides describe a game that no longer exists
disclosures.body: Update 36.0 (2024-06-18) gutted the Voidrig recipe. Scintillant, Stellated Necrathene, Cranial Foremount, Thaumic Distillate, Trapezium Xenorhast and Cabochon Embolos are all gone; everything mined for it now is common or uncommon.

disclosures.title: buying instead of farming
disclosures.body: Built Voidrig components sell for roughly 60-100 platinum each on Warframe Market, and several players find it faster to farm relics for that plat than to farm the mech directly. The trade-off: that route skips the Necramech mods and Entrati rank the quest chain still requires.
